lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.25 - A Listen and say. Then practise.

details: Listen and say introduces new adjectives for describing feelings. Then practise provides initial practice of the grammar structure used to ask and answer questions about how someone felt when something happened.
Look for clear pronunciation of the six feeling adjectives and accurate repetition of the target question and 'I felt...' answer structure.

“Last week I argued with my friend. Do you remember? Can you guess how I felt? That’s right… I was very upset. But then I won my football game! And I felt really confident. How about you? Can you talk about how things made you feel? Let’s try!”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.25 - B. Write. Then ask and answer.

details: Write. Then ask and answer provides structured practice of the target language. Students first write to connect the events to the feelings, then use their written work to support a spoken dialogue with a partner.
Look for correctly completed sentences in writing. Then, listen for accurate use of the target question and answer structure during the pair work activity.

“Excellent! So how did you feel when you passed a test? How about when you lost a book? Let’s see if you can write down the words for the pictures, and don’t forget to ask your friend too! And you can ask me!”

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.87 - A Circle and write.

details: Circle and write consolidates the spelling of the new feeling adjectives. Students use the picture clues to find and circle the correct word in a letter string, then write it correctly.
Look for the correct word circled in each letter string and accurately spelled on the corresponding line.
“The words for our feelings are hidden inside these long strings of letters! Can you be a word detective, find the right feeling for each picture, and then write it down for me?”

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.87 - B Look at A and write. Then match.

details: Look at A and write. Then match provides comprehensive practice of the lesson's target language. Students write the feeling, then match it to the past event that caused it, reinforcing the full sentence structure.
Look for correctly written feeling adjectives and accurately drawn lines connecting each feeling to the appropriate past event.

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.26 - Speaking Board Game

details: The Board Game provides a fun, communicative context for fluency practice. The game encourages students to spontaneously connect past events with feelings, consolidating the lesson's grammar and vocabulary.
Look for active participation from all students, correct use of the question and answer structures, and clear pronunciation of the feeling adjectives and past events.

“You know I love playing games. Do you want to play a game too? Great! We can use the pictures to talk about our feelings and what happened. Keep an eye out for the bonus car to jump ahead! The first person to reach the finish line is the winner. Good luck!”
